features.note: Form unchanged; wordmark now reads upright (see mount-trim-ring).
Interior still legible through the (now smoked) bubble at unchanged opacity 0.42; optics 43/43 reachable in all four states.

THE FIX THAT MATTERS. A near-white bubble (#dfe6ea) at E=1.715 contributed 1.342 of its OWN screen luminance, dominating the alpha mix, so the matte black shroud behind it came through at 0.671 screen = 76% of the white collar beside it — the optical cavity stopped reading as a cavity and the dome read as a LUMINAIRE, the exact failure the black shroud exists to prevent. The critical was being defeated by the piece IN FRONT of it. Fix: smoked bubble #8a949c -> the veiled cavity lands at 0.335 = 38% of the collar, reading as a cavity again, WITHOUT changing opacity (interior no less visible; the bubble just stops glowing over it). Defensible too: security domes are smoked precisely so the lens aim can't be read, and the tint was already an unpublished open item with clear-vs-smoked flagged as a real product difference — now measured-as-necessary.

WORDMARK FIXED and CONFIRMED. The 'AXIS' letters now read upright (A->X->I->S left-to-right along the plate) — verified in an orchestrator crop of the under view. Resolved by CALCULATION, not guessing: the check projects the mapped face's U and V axes to screen and computes text advance; the real bug was GEOMETRY (on a BoxGeometry -y face U runs along local X, V along local Z; the plate's length was in z so the text ran up V, bottom-to-top). Length moved to local X + plate rotated 90deg -> text runs along U with TEXT_ROT 0, world position/bbox unchanged. The residual tilt is perspective on a tangential plate, not a defect (the criterion was also corrected: advance within 60deg of horizontal, not-upside-down, AND must fit the long canvas axis).

important_features.note: FIXED through the tone curve. At emissiveIntensity 1.0 the ON LED rendered 0.620 screen vs the 0.879 housing around it — a lit lamp DARKER than its own bezel reads OFF; the linear numbers didn't flag it because collar and lamp fall on opposite sides of the ACES knee and compression reordered them. Raised to 4.0 -> 0.914 (brighter than the bezel). The CEILING is recorded in the spec: ACES compression means even intensity 8 stays under 1.11x the collar, so a later pass must not push past 4 expecting a gain the curve can't give; the rest of the read comes from HUE (saturated green vs neutral white), which a luma metric cannot see.

defects: The standalone framing-probe reports overlapsHUD:true / mis-composed, but that is a FALSE POSITIVE: it tests the projected bbox AABB, whose top-right corner (ndc 0.65, 0.94) falls in the PROCEDENCIA panel zone, while the ROUND dome's silhouette does not reach there. Orchestrator pixel measurement: at the panel's x-columns the panel bottom is y~987-991 and the topmost trim-ring pixel is y~1010 (or absent) — a ~23 px gap, no real overlap. The builder's __qaFraming check ('free of HUD') is correct. Tooling note: the bbox-based HUD-overlap test over-reports on round/domed subjects (bbox is not the silhouette).
Screws still NOT built (correct); smoked tint remains an open item (now measured-as-necessary).
corrections: Do NOT raise the LED intensity past 4 (ACES ceiling recorded); do not un-smoke the bubble (it defeats the cavity).

mechanical.notes: 10/10 suites (adds orient + tonemap). Console clean. THE INSTRUMENT CHANGED and drove everything: all prior measurements on this asset compared LINEAR luminance, but the renderer applies ACES at exposure 1.05, which compresses the highs hard — two linearly-separated values can land together on screen and a linearly-tuned value can look nothing like its number. Judging THROUGH the ACES fit (Narkowicz, the curve three.js uses) surfaced two defects every linear measurement had passed: the LED darker than its bezel, and the bubble defeating the cavity. Verified: LED on 0.914 vs housing 0.879; cavity 0.335 vs collar 0.879 (38%); optics 43/43 through transparent surfaces only in all four states; rig unchanged (down-normals 1.715 vs up 0.094, four lamps below, metalness untouched); wordmark runs along the long canvas axis and reads upright in hero (advance 24deg) and under (50deg). Framing: fullyVisible/centered/wellFramed; overlapsHUD is a bbox-vs-silhouette false positive (measured 23 px gap).

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The pass's methodological advance is the point: judging THROUGH the ACES tone curve rather than in linear caught two defects that every linear measurement had greenlit — a lit LED darker than its own bezel (reordered across the curve's knee) and, the important one, a near-white bubble whose own luminance drowned the black shroud so the dome read as a luminaire instead of a camera (the critical defeated by the piece in front of it — smoked, opacity unchanged, cavity restored). The wordmark was resolved by projecting the face's UV axes to screen rather than trial-and-error, and the geometry, not the canvas, turned out to be the bug. I resolved the framing-probe's overlapsHUD flag as a bbox-not-silhouette false positive by measuring the pixels (23 px gap). Cleared to the interaction-ui pass; the ACES ceiling on the LED and the smoked tint are both recorded so a later pass does not undo them.
